$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.22,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.22/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 40f7bca8563d03c77f3f8680a50b01e8820c39f3ef2c3772cce23ffd7ef65c31 and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.22/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
40f7bca8563d03c77f3f8680a50b01e8820c39f3ef2c3772cce23ffd7ef65c31 is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
